title: September temperature gave no clear autumn interval forecast gain beyond trends in eight Japan tests in 1989-2025
abstract: We tested whether September mean temperature improves later-year forecasts of the time from leaf colour to leaf fall. We used JMA ginkgo and maple records and GHCN-CAMS temperature. Each fit used earlier years only. The selected panel had 6,186 paired records at 62 distinct stations. Tests used 2,555 tree-type station-years in North and South Japan in 1989-2006 and 2007-2025. Adding temperature to station and observation-category intercepts and a common time trend changed mean squared interval error by -2.40% to +1.42%, where positive values mean lower error. All eight adjusted uncertainty intervals included zero. Separate local trends gave the same null conclusion. A baseline without a trend gave larger gains. The result shows no clear added interval forecast value for this predictor and model. It does not show that temperature has no effect. Selected coverage, missing visit and tree histories, coarse weather data and short test periods limit inference. The package contains source hashes, code, paired evidence, predictions and uncertainty estimates.

display.caption: Adding September temperature to a trend baseline gave no clear interval forecast gain. Positive skill means lower mean squared error. Bars are marginal 95 percent intervals, not the eight-test adjusted intervals used for the primary conclusion.

citations.reason: Prior trends in the same JMA colour-to-fall intervals. This study tests earlier-month prediction in later years.
Prior temperature-contrast study identified post-event exposure in fixed autumn windows. September-only prediction avoids that timing problem in these test records.
Prior ginkgo interval slope study. The data overlap; this is not independent biological evidence.
